name: hcapp_reactToChatMessage
description: Adds or removes the caller's emoji reaction on a chat message of any thread kind — run, kennel, room or DM (E9.F1.S22, 2026-09-30). The rule and the write live in HC6.nonApi_reactToChatMessage (same visibility as the thread's readers; a blocked author, a removed message or an unknown reaction code is refused); this SP authenticates, maps the outcome to an envelope, and hands the API what it needs to nudge the message's author. Auth: HC6.ValidateAppAuth (spNumber 140, @param NULL — a standard token). Permission gate: inside nonApi_reactToChatMessage, from the token's user. ReactionsJson is keyed by catalog code (HC6.ChatReactionCatalog: thumbs, heart, laugh, beer, run, fire), not by emoji, because an emoji equals '' in this collation. Uses the two-rowset error shape: {success 0, errorCode, errorType} then the standard error detail.

parameters.name: deviceId
parameters.description: Registered device UUID. Default NULL (ValidateAppAuth then fails gracefully).

parameters.name: accessToken
parameters.description: Short-lived token (standard, device secret; @param NULL). Default NULL.

parameters.name: messageId
parameters.description: The message reacted to. Required; NULL → 1990. Unknown or removed → 1991.

parameters.name: reaction
parameters.description: A code from HC6.ChatReactionCatalog(): thumbs, heart, laugh, beer, run, fire. Required; NULL → 1990. Not in the catalog → 1993. Stored as a key in EventMessage.ReactionsJson.

parameters.name: on
parameters.description: 1 add (default) / 0 remove. Not validated: any value other than 1 (including NULL) removes.

rowsets.description: Auth failure only (ValidateAppAuth): the error detail is returned ALONE at index 0 and the SP returns — no envelope precedes it.

rowsets.name: ErrorEnvelope
rowsets.description: Every other refusal: {success 0, errorCode, errorType} at index 0, followed by the StandardErrorResult detail at index 1. Codes: 1990 missing messageId/reaction (errorType 2); 1991 message not found or removed (3); 1992 not allowed — the caller cannot see the thread or the author has blocked them (3); 1993 unknown reaction code (3); 1994 unhandled error from the CATCH (5).

columns.name: errorType
columns.description: 2 validation, 3 not found / not allowed, 5 unhandled.

rowsets.description: Follows the ErrorEnvelope on every non-auth refusal.

columns.name: reactions
columns.description: EventMessage.ReactionsJson after the change, e.g. {"beer":["<PublicHasherId>",...]}; NULL when no reactions remain.

rowsets.name: PushDetail
rowsets.description: On success, API ONLY (stripped before the reply): where the message lives, in the keys the app's open chat page matches a push on. One row.

columns.name: RoomType
columns.description: EventMessage.MessageType, only when EventId, KennelId and ThreadId are all NULL (a global room).

rowsets.name: SilentRecipients
rowsets.description: On success, API ONLY: the message AUTHOR's mobile devices (IsMobile 1, removed 0, FcmToken present, build >= HC6.MinBuildForChatPush()) — never the reactor's own (empty when the reactor is the author). A data-only push so an open thread refreshes; nobody is buzzed for a beer. No 180-day idle cut-off here, unlike the message sends.

sideEffects: EXEC HC6.nonApi_reactToChatMessage — UPDATE HC.EventMessage.ReactionsJson and ReactionsUpdatedAt (outcome 1); nothing written for outcomes 2–4.
INSERT HC.ErrorLog on 1990 and on every nonApi refusal (1991–1993), and in the CATCH (1994).
The API shim sends a silent FCM data push (Type=reaction) to the author's phones from rowset 2; nothing is queued in the database.

codeSmells.detail: Line 6 defaults @on to 1 and nothing checks it is 0 or 1; HC6.nonApi_reactToChatMessage (its line 101) treats anything but 1 as a remove. A client sending NULL or 2 silently removes a reaction instead of being refused.

codeSmells.issue: Success RETURN inside the TRY after three rowsets
codeSmells.detail: Line 108 RETURNs from inside BEGIN TRY after rowsets 0–2 have been sent. A failure in the push-detail or recipients SELECTs (lines 88–107) lands in the CATCH, which then appends {success 0, 1994} AFTER a {success 1} rowset the client has already received — contradictory rowsets for a reaction that was saved. The sends (hcapp_sendRoomMessage) isolate push plumbing in its own swallow TRY.

breakingChangeRules: Never remove a column from any rowset
Never change a sentinel value meaning
Never change errorType integer codes without updating all callers
